summary: The Posts lane is Insidor's front door: a 40-row ranked terminal board of individual viral posts, scored on a per-author-normalised burst rate rather than raw reach, showing each post 20–90 minutes before a coin exists for it. Its one job is to answer "what is going viral right now, and how much head start do I still have on it" at post granularity — before clustering, before a story, before a ticker. Every row resolves to a single primary action that is a pure function of the CONFIRMED coin count on the post's story (zero for an unclustered post, which is the normal case here), so the ambiguous "buy which one?" state is never rendered.
mechanism:
═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. THE RANKING FORMULA
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Reuses the single ranking primitive from docs/research/03-system-design.md §4.2, specialised to one post. Both lanes share code; only the aggregation differs.

  base      = rate_LCB_norm × burst^0.5
  PostHeat  = (base × O)^0.85 / ((age_min + 12)/12)^1.35 × C × E

  D (author-diversity) = 1.0 for a single post, by definition (§4.2).

TERMS
─────
rate_LCB_norm — Gamma-Poisson lower confidence bound on VIEW arrival rate, normalised.

  λ | data  ~ Gamma(a₀ + V(t), b₀ + t)
  rate_LCB  = Gamma⁻¹(0.10 ; a₀ + V(t), b₀ + t)          [views/min]
  rate_LCB_norm = rate_LCB / platform_norms.median_view_rate_24h

  (a₀, b₀) come from the author's follower-decile bucket in author_roster. The
  prior IS the cold-start answer — no null, no blind window. This kills the
  3→30 false positive, prices in bought views (the LCB punishes small n), and
  is scale-aware without being scale-dominated.

burst — continuous-time EWMA ratio. NOT a discrete α·x + (1−α)·S, which is
  wrong under the irregular 4/9/14/21/30/42/58/78-minute snapshot grid and
  biases hot-tier posts upward by construction.

  S ← S·exp(−Δt/τ) + (1 − exp(−Δt/τ))·(ΔV/Δt)
  burst = S_fast / max(S_slow, ε)     τ_fast = 20 min, τ_slow = 6 h

  Scale-free: a 300-follower account spiking can outrank a 500k account's
  baseline traffic. And it is the one thing an HN-shaped score provably cannot
  do — detect a SECOND WAVE, which is the dominant pattern in memecoin attention.
  The ^0.5 exponent keeps a 9× burst from being 9× the score.

O ∈ [0.15, 1.0] — organic multiplier, five features, all computable from
  post_snapshots we already collect at zero marginal cost (§4.5):

  F1 STEP        maxShare = max(deltas)/sum(deltas)
                 f1 = clamp(1 − (maxShare − 0.45)/0.40, 0.10, 1)
  F2 DEPTH       lv = likes/views
                 f2 = lv<0.0015 ? 0.25 : lv<0.004 ? 0.6 : clamp(lv/0.01, 0.6, 1.15)
  F3 CONVO       rl = replies/likes
                 f3 = rl<0.005 ? 0.5 : clamp(0.7 + 4·rl, 0.7, 1.2)
  F4 PLAUSIBLE   overshoot = views/followers_at_post
                 f4 = (overshoot > 200 && quotes < 5) ? 0.35 : 1
  F5 MONOTONE    f5 = any(delta < 0) ? 0.7 : 1
  O = clamp(f1·f2·f3·f4·f5, 0.15, 1.0)

  Multiplicative (failing one test caps the score), floored at 0.15 not 0 — a
  false positive demotes rather than erases. Every O < 0.5 is logged with its
  per-feature breakdown so the failures are auditable, not invisible.

C — crypto-pickup penalty. 0.35 once ≥3 distinct crypto-native accounts have
  quoted/replied to THIS post; else 1.0. This is the formula's expression of the
  product thesis: the moment CT finds it, our edge is gone and it should fall
  off the board even while still growing. No competitor's ranking does this
  because no competitor claims earliness.

E — entry-integrity multiplier. 1.0 normally; 0.70 when censored_entry = true.
  ⚠ TUNABLE, currently a judgement call, not a fitted value — see open questions.

α = 0.85, γ = 1.35, t₀ = 12 min are the tuning surface. At these values the age
penalty is 2.27 at t=10min and 25.5 at t=120min, ratio 11.2 → the older post needs
11.2^(1/0.85) = 17.1× the momentum to overtake. The board turns over in ~40 min.

PRESENTED HEAT (the 0–100 in the HEAT column)
  presented_heat = round(100 · min(1, PostHeat / platform_norms.p95_heat_1h))
  Self-calibrating: a dead night still shows spread, a wild night isn't all 100s.

ELIGIBILITY GATE (all must hold — §4.3, post lane)
  age_min ≤ 240
  rate_LCB_reshares ≥ floor_absolute       ← reshares, not views. Views never gate.
  cumulative_views ≥ platform floor
  meme_score ≥ 0.35
  O ≥ 0.30
  coinability ≠ 'blocked'
  author appears < 3× in the current top 20
  ticks_qualified ≥ 2

Cumulative reach is an ELIGIBILITY GATE, not the ranking base and not a fallback
ranking term. This is what FAST_LANE_VIEWS / views/1000 must be refactored into.

───────────────────────────────────────────
THE THREE HARD CASES
───────────────────────────────────────────

(a) FIRST SEEN WHEN ALREADY LARGE — "censored entry"

  Detection, at first snapshot:
    censored_entry = (V₀ > 5 × platform_median_views_at_age(τ₀))
                     OR (first_seen_at − posted_at > 20 min)

  Consequences, all of them:
    · rate seeded as V₀ / max(τ₀, 1) — a cumulative-derived rate, so it ranks
      correctly instead of near-zero. (Fixes velocity.js:50 returning null.)
    · burst := 1.0 until the second observation — we have no history, so we
      assert nothing.
    · E = 0.70. We cannot verify the growth is happening now rather than
      already having happened, and the product's entire claim is "now".
    · earliness_eligible = false, PERMANENTLY. Excluded from the lead-time
      denominator. Any other choice makes the headline metric a lie.
    · Row renders an amber `ALREADY HOT` .lc-pill and its AGE cell carries no
      lead figure — never a fake "+31m early".
    · It may never fire an alert on its own; it is a board row, not a signal.

(b) DECELERATING POST — three independent layers, in order of speed

  1. burst falls first. A post peaking at 30 min and cooling at 60 min has
     S_fast collapsing while S_slow lags → burst ≈ 0.3 → burst^0.5 = 0.55.
     The ACCEL column shows `0.3×` in --dim. Visible before the rank moves.
  2. Age penalty compounds: (72/12)^1.35 = 10.9 vs (22/12)^1.35 = 2.32.
  3. Lifecycle, with hysteresis (§2.5), governs EXIT not score:
       HEATING if R̂ ≥ 1.15 OR (g ≥ +0.020 AND v ≥ 0.5 reshares/min)
       COOLING if v < 0.60·v_peak AND g ≤ −0.010, for 2 consecutive snaps
       DEAD    if v < 0.05·v_peak OR (v < 0.2 AND τ > 90)
     COOLING → exits after EXIT_TICKS = 3 (60 s). DEAD → exits immediately,
     bypassing EXIT_TICKS. COOLING→HEATING is forbidden unless v re-exceeds
     0.80·v_peak — that is what stops the lifecycle pill from flickering.

  SECOND WAVE re-entry: an exited post re-enters if burst ≥ 1.6 and it
  re-qualifies for 2 ticks. It gets a cyan `2ND WAVE` .lc-pill and keeps its
  original posted_at (so the age penalty still applies honestly — a second
  wave on a 3-hour-old post has to be genuinely violent to make the board).
  This is the case the entire EWMA-over-HN argument exists to serve.

(c) COLD START — exactly one snapshot

  base is computable at snapshot 1: rate_LCB from the Gamma-Poisson posterior
  with the follower-decile prior, burst := 1.0 (neutral, asserts nothing).
  There is no null and no 20/60-minute blind window.

  But ticks_qualified = 0, so it CANNOT enter the board until 2 consecutive
  20 s commits — 40 s of dwell. On a product whose claim is earliness, 40 s is
  real money, so there is an escape hatch:

    if rate_LCB_reshares ≥ HARD_ENTER_FLOOR → enter on tick 1, skip the dwell,
    render the lime `NEW` .narr-new-pin chip for 120 s.

  A single-snapshot post never shows an ACCEL value (renders `—`, never `1.0×`
  — a fabricated 1.0 reads as "flat", which is a different claim from "unknown")
  and its sparkline cell renders the .qthumb-style empty treatment, not a flat line.

───────────────────────────────────────────
RECOMPUTE CADENCE — three tiers, deliberately decreasing volatility outward
───────────────────────────────────────────

| Layer                    | Cadence            | Mechanism                        |
|--------------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------|
| Accumulator (S_fast/slow,| on snapshot arrival| pipeline writes post_heat        |
| O features, counters)    | (4,9,14,21,30,42…) |                                  |
| Heat refresh             | 60 s               | pg_cron, one SQL UPDATE          |
| Rank commit              | 20 s               | commit_board() + board_ticks row |
| Delta push to clients    | on change, ≤1/500ms| Supabase Broadcast `board:posts` |
| platform_norms (median,  | hourly             | pg_cron                          |
| p95_heat_1h)             |                    |                                  |

The principle, stated so it can be defended: **the faster a quantity changes,
the less it is allowed to move the page.** Raw counters tick on arrival, heat
recomputes at 60 s, rank commits at 20 s but only moves when the stability
rules allow. Two of every three commits see identical heat — that is the point.

OUTAGE HANDLING: on a detected ingestion gap, FREEZE the EWMA state (do not
decay it) and amortise the accumulated delta over the true elapsed dt on
resumption. Otherwise the original failure recurs inverted — a wave of fake
bursts instead of an empty page. Affected rows render a `FROZEN` chip and their
HEAT cell goes --dim; the ledger marks the window unmeasurable, not a win.

───────────────────────────────────────────
RANK CHURN PREVENTION — five server rules + three UI rules
───────────────────────────────────────────

Server (commit_board(), every 20 s):
  EPS_SWAP    = 0.08     challenger must beat incumbent heat by 8% to pass it
  ENTER_TICKS = 2        consecutive qualifying ticks to enter
  EXIT_TICKS  = 3        consecutive sub-threshold ticks to leave
  PIN_MS      = 90_000   minimum dwell once on board
  MAX_MOVE    = 5        max rank positions moved per tick

Structural caps applied inside the same commit: max 2 rows per author in the
top 20; max 1 row per story (see §6); near-duplicate media collapse at
hamming(media_phash) ≤ 6.

UI:
  · FREEZE ON HOVER. While the pointer is inside the table, reorders queue and
    apply on mouseleave. The table gains a 1px inset rgba(61,224,255,.25) ring
    and the control strip shows a mono `PAUSED · 3 QUEUED` micro-label.
  · NEVER REFLOW BELOW THE FOLD. New entrants that would land above row 12
    batch into a sticky `.newpill` under the header — `↑ 3 new` in --ion —
    which applies on click and scrolls to top.
  · VALUES UPDATE LIVE; POSITIONS DO NOT. Row values come from a
    Map<post_id, Row> updated every push unconditionally. Only the ordering
    array is held. This is the single most important implementation rule on
    the surface: the numbers are always current even when the board is frozen.

───────────────────────────════════════════
2. THE STORY RELATIONSHIP — the feed does NOT collapse posts into stories live
═══════════════════════════════════════════

Decision: a post row NEVER disappears because a background job clustered it.
Three reasons, in order of weight:
  1. A row vanishing under the cursor is the worst instance of the exact
     failure the whole stability section exists to prevent.
  2. Clustering runs an LLM adjudicator in an 8–12% uncertainty band. A wrong
     merge that silently removes a post the user was tracking is unrecoverable
     from the UI — there is no "where did it go".
  3. The posts lane's job is post granularity. The stories lane already exists
     for the aggregate. Two lanes, two granularities, both true.

What actually happens when narrative_posts.narrative_id is set:
  · The row STAYS IN PLACE and gains a `→ STORY` chip in its chip line,
    linking to the story. No reorder, no flash on the row itself.
  · The ACTION button re-resolves against the STORY's confirmed coin count.
    This can flip `Create coin` → `Buy $TICKER` in place. That flip gets a
    one-time 850 ms --ion pulse on the button — the single most important
    state change on this surface, and the only thing on the row permitted to
    animate for a reason other than a number changing.
  · The row's stable key changes from post:<id> to story:<narrative_id>.
  · SECOND AND LATER members of the same story do NOT each get a row.
    ONE ROW PER STORY, held by the highest-heat member. Later members fold
    into it as a `+4 posts` chip; their bases contribute to the story's heat
    (in the stories lane) but never create a second post row. This is the
    honest collapse: it stops the board being twelve rows of the same TikTok
    without any row ever vanishing.
  · If the highest-heat member changes, the row identity is stable and the
    thumbnail + author line crossfade over 850 ms. Never a reorder.
  · If a merge is later reversed, the post re-enters as its own row with
    ENTER_TICKS waived.

`COLLAPSE BY STORY` is a control-strip toggle, default ON. OFF shows every post
as its own row and adds a colour-keyed 3px left `.storydot` marker so duplicates
are visually grouped without being merged — a power-user affordance for someone
auditing whether the clusterer is right.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. MEDIA — three cases, handled honestly
═══════════════════════════════════════════

CASE 1 — IMAGE. `img.memeimg` in a 44×44 `.qthumb`, object-fit cover,
  loading="lazy", src = narrative_posts.media_url. Hover with 400 ms dwell
  opens a 320px preview popover (not a modal, not a nav). Never upscaled.

CASE 2 — VIDEO (TikTok, X native). Poster frame from
  narrative_posts.media_poster_url ⚠ (does not exist) + `.play-mini` 22px
  overlay + `.srcchip-mini` reading `from video` (SRCLABEL already has this).
  If no poster frame exists, fall back to the `.qthumb .ph` gradient
  placeholder driven by --p1/--p2/--p3 from PAL(1–6), seeded by post id.

CASE 3 — NO MEDIA. `.qthumb .ph` gradient + `.srcchip-mini` reading `no media`.
  Link-preview case → `from link`. Media-in-replies case → `from replies`.

⚠ CORRECTION TO THE EXISTING COMPONENT: kill the
`loremflickr.com/80/80/<keyword>` → `picsum.photos/seed/<seed>/80` fallback
chain in the current narrative thumbnail (§4.3 of the component inventory).
Fabricating stock media on a terminal whose thesis is 0.97 precision is a lie
told in pixels. The PAL gradient is the correct empty state — it is visually
distinct, deterministic per post, and claims nothing.

TIKTOK'S SPECIFIC PROBLEM — the meme is in the video, the caption is hashtag spam.
  · The caption renders VERBATIM. Hashtag tokens are styled at --dim while the
    rest is --ink. That is presentation, not alteration.
  · If alpha_ratio(caption) < 0.35 (i.e. it is mostly hashtags), the text line
    instead renders post_derived_subject ⚠ (does not exist) — Insidor's own
    one-line description of the video — prefixed with a mono 9px `DERIVED`
    micro-label in --dim so it can never be mistaken for the author's words.
    The verbatim caption is still shown in full in the detail sheet.
  · TikTok rows carry `shares / likes / views` in the detail sheet, not
    `reposts / replies / views` — the platform's engagement grammar differs and
    mapping them onto each other loses information.

X DISPLAY CONSTRAINTS — structural, not cosmetic:
  · Post text is rendered UNALTERED. We visually clip with CSS text-overflow;
    we never truncate or edit server-side, and the full text is one click away.
  · Author name and @handle link to https://x.com/<handle>. The `.pbadge` X
    mark is the attribution mark and is always present.
  · The timestamp links to the permalink
    https://x.com/<handle>/status/<platform_post_id>,
    target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer".
  · NO THIRD-PARTY ACTION CONTROLS ATTACHED TO A RENDERED POST. This drives
    the layout: the ACTION button lives in its own grid cell, outside the
    post-content cell, separated by a 1px --line divider. It is never a
    like/repost/reply/follow control — `Create coin` and `Buy $TICKER` are
    Insidor actions on an Insidor object (the story, the coin), not engagement
    actions on the post. The engagement counts in the detail sheet are text,
    never buttons.
  · Metrics shown are the current values from the last snapshot, and the
    row's staleness is surfaced (LAST TICK indicator) rather than silently
    presenting old counts as live.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. THE ACTION — the one rule, applied to a pre-coin object
═══════════════════════════════════════════

The primary button is a pure function of the CONFIRMED coin count on the post's
STORY. A post with no story has no story-coins, so n = 0 by construction —
which is why the overwhelming majority of this board reads `Create coin`, and
that is correct: this is the surface where you are early enough that nothing
exists yet.

| Post state                                  | n | Primary button      |
|---------------------------------------------|---|---------------------|
| Unclustered (narrative_id null)             | 0 | `Create coin`       |
| Clustered, story has 0 confirmed coins      | 0 | `Create coin`       |
| Clustered, story has 1 confirmed coin       | 1 | `Buy $TICKER`       |
| Clustered, story has ≥2 confirmed coins     | n | `See the 3 coins`   |
| Story has only UNSURE candidates            | 0 | `Create coin` + muted, non-actionable candidate line below |
| coinability = 'no_create' (D3 tier 2)       | — | no button; `NOT MINTABLE` chip |
| coinability = 'blocked' (D3 tier 1)         | — | row does not exist  |

ABSTAIN, precisely (D1 + §5.9): when the story's best coin match is UNSURE, the
Buy button is SUPPRESSED — but the candidate mint is still SHOWN, in the action
cell's second line, as `$KANG · unverified` in --muted with a --line border,
opening a coin page carrying a persistent warning banner and a Buy control that
requires a second explicit confirm. Abstain never means hide. Confidence is
rendered CATEGORICALLY — never "73% match" next to an actionable control,
because users treat 73% as good enough and do their own thresholding, which
defeats the abstain band entirely.

`Create coin` prefills from post_meme_scores.suggested_ticker /
suggested_name / the post media. This is THE ONLY PLACE the LLM-suggested
ticker belongs — it must never reach ticker enrichment or narrative_tickers
(that is the live $KANG bug, cluster.js:310).

WALLET NOT CONNECTED: the button renders its TRUE label and is fully enabled;
clicking opens Privy, then completes the original intent. Never grey out the
primary action for auth — that hides what the product would do and costs the
normie user the entire flow.

Secondary actions, all outside the post-content cell: row body click opens the
post detail sheet (.pd-sheet); `.star` toggles watchlist (keyed to post_id
while unclustered, migrating to narrative_id on cluster).

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. LIVE BEHAVIOUR
═══════════════════════════════════════════

ANIMATES:
  · Numeric cells REACH, RATE, HEAT on value change — `.nm-tick-up` (lime,
    translateY 4px→0, 850 ms) / `.nm-tick-down` (red, −4px→0). Class removed
    at 900 ms. Existing component, reused verbatim.
  · New entrant — `.narr-flash` 1.4s lime wash + `.ntk.narr-pinned` 3px lime
    inset left rail + `NEW` `.narr-new-pin` chip for 120 s (NOT the current
    300 s pin — that is longer than the board's own 40-minute turnover).
  · Rank movement — the `#` cell shows `▲2` / `▼1` in lime/red for one tick
    (20 s) then fades to plain. THE ROW ITSELF DOES NOT SLIDE.
  · The action button, once, on a coin-count transition (850 ms --ion pulse).
  · The `.lz` live dot and `.narr-live-dot` pulse, 2 s, as already specified.

MUST NOT ANIMATE:
  · Row reordering. Reorder is a single atomic swap on the tick boundary. No
    FLIP, no transition, never while frozen, never below the fold.
  · Row height. Chips appearing (→ STORY, 2ND WAVE, +4 posts) must not reflow
    the row — the chip line is a fixed-height 16px slot, always present.
  · Thumbnails. No autoplay video on the board — bandwidth and attention.
  · The page. No spinner on refresh; every update is a diff.

HOW A USER WHO HAS WATCHED FOR TEN MINUTES KNOWS WHAT CHANGED — three mechanisms:

  1. SINCE OPEN. A session baseline t_open is captured on mount. The control
     strip toggle switches REACH and RATE to deltas since t_open (`+840K`
     rather than `2.4M`) and draws a 1px --ion hairline between rows that
     existed at t_open and rows that entered after. Default off, session-scoped.
  2. Δ10m RANK MODE. The `#` cell's caret is normally relative to the previous
     commit; the toggle makes it relative to 10 minutes ago, computed from
     board_ticks. `▲14` over ten minutes is a different fact from `▲2` over
     twenty seconds and the board should be able to say both.
  3. THE RAIL, in Posts mode, is an append-only chronological log of BOARD
     EVENTS — not posts. `ENTERED #7 · @handle`, `LEFT · cooling`,
     `2ND WAVE · #12`, `CT PICKUP · 3 accounts`, `CLUSTERED → story`,
     `SNAPSHOT GAP · 4m`. This is the "what changed" ledger, and it is the
     thing a competitor's feed structurally cannot show, because they have no
     board state to log transitions against.

Plus a permanent honesty instrument in the control strip: `LAST TICK 4s` in
mono --dim, turning amber at >45 s and red at >120 s, at which point a
`.scoring-paused-banner`-styled amber bar reads
`PIPELINE STALE — last snapshot 6m ago. Ranks are frozen.` The existing
`Meme scoring paused / Anthropic budget exhausted` banner is retained verbatim.

DELIVERY: Supabase Broadcast on topic `board:posts`, change-driven with
per-client coalescing to at most one frame per 500 ms. Payload is a diff:
`{tick, changes:[{id, rank, prev_rank, heat, views, rate, burst, lifecycle}],
enters:[fullRow], exits:[id]}` — full row only on enter. Postgres Changes is
disqualified (5 changes/sec ceiling under RLS at 4k clients). Hydration and
disconnect fallback is an ISR route with `revalidate = 2` and JITTERED client
polling — never clock-aligned, which deterministically serves everyone the
stale copy.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. FILTERS AND SORTS — the governing rule
═══════════════════════════════════════════

FILTERS CHANGE THE SET. SORTS CHANGE THE ORDER. THE ELIGIBILITY GATE APPLIES
TO BOTH. A user sorting by NEW still sees only gated posts — otherwise "newest"
returns 40,000 pieces of junk and the product looks broken. The one exception
is SHOW RISKY, which relaxes a hard gate and is therefore a visually loud
toggle, never a checkbox in a drawer.

When a sort or filter is active and the gate is removing items, the strip
shows `12 hidden by gate` as a --dim mono link opening a per-reason breakdown
(meme_score 7, O 3, author cap 2). D2 applied to the board itself: the user can
always see what we suppressed and why.

screens.name: Live Feed — Posts lane (the board)
screens.job: Rank the 40 posts that are going viral right now, so a trader can decide within one row-scan whether to act before anyone else has seen it.
screens.layout:
Reuses `.shell` — main column 1fr + `aside.rail` 460px (rail hidden ≤1040px). Nav `.nav` 58px sticky. CONTROL STRIP sticky at top:58px, height 44px, `background:rgba(6,6,7,.82); backdrop-filter:blur(14px); border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)`. Board is a `.ttable` (existing shell: `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,.018), transparent 100px), var(--bg1)`, 1px rgba(255,255,255,.055), radius 14, inset highlight + 0 20px 50px -30px shadow) with a sticky `.pthd` header at top:102px.

GRID (header `.pthd` and row `.ptk` share it, modelled on `.nthd`/`.ntk`):
`display:grid; grid-template-columns: 30px minmax(320px,2.6fr) 58px .72fr .82fr .6fr 84px .5fr .58fr 52px 96px; gap:12px; align-items:center; padding:10px 20px; min-height:64px;`

Eleven columns: # · POST · HEAT · REACH · RATE · ACCEL · 20M · ORG · MEME · AGE · (action, unlabelled header).
Header spans: `font-size:10px; color:var(--dim); text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.08em; font-weight:600`. Numeric cells right-aligned, `var(--mono)`, 12.5px, tabular-nums. `.sortable` + `i.sar` arrows (▼/▲) exactly as `bindThdSort`.
Responsive `.h` classes: hide 20M + ORG ≤1180px; additionally hide ACCEL + MEME ≤1040px (down to 7 columns).
Row hover `background:rgba(61,224,255,.04)`; separator `inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.035)`.
Board is capped at 40 rows. Below it: a `.noresult`-styled footer line `40 of 63 eligible · 12 hidden by gate`.

elements.shows: Integer 1–40 in mono 11px --dim, plus a one-tick movement caret `▲2` (lime) / `▼1` (red) that fades to plain after 20s. In Δ10m mode the caret is relative to ten minutes ago.
elements.source: board_state.rank, board_state.prev_rank ⚠ (table does not exist); Δ10m from board_ticks lookback ⚠ (does not exist)
elements.interaction: Not clickable. The caret is the only movement indicator — rows never physically slide.

elements.shows: 44×44 `.qthumb` (radius 8). Image → img.memeimg cover. Video → poster frame + `.play-mini` 22px + `.srcchip-mini` `from video`. Nothing → `.qthumb .ph` PAL gradient (--p1/--p2/--p3 seeded by post id) + `.srcchip-mini` `no media`.
elements.source: narrative_posts.media_url, narrative_posts.media_type, narrative_posts.media_poster_url ⚠ (does not exist), PAL(1–6) keyed on hash(post.id)
elements.interaction: Hover 400ms → 320px preview popover. Click → post permalink in a new tab (this is the post-content region, so linking out is correct).

elements.shows: `.pbadge` 18px platform mark · `.who` display name 12.5px 600 --ink · `.at` @handle 10.5px mono --muted · `· 412K` follower count, mono 10.5px --dim. Follower count is inline rather than a column because it is static, never sorted, and only exists to answer 'is this a big account's normal traffic or a small account going nuclear' — which is the F4 overshoot denominator.

elements.shows: burst as a multiple: `3.2×`. Lime ≥1.3, amber 0.8–1.3, --dim <0.8. Renders `—` when only one snapshot exists — never a fabricated `1.0×`. This is the deceleration column: the trader's single most important question is 'is it still going', and burst answers it 40+ seconds before the rank moves.
elements.interaction: Sortable. Hover → 'accelerating 3.2× above its 6h baseline'.

Shape is the point — one vertical step then flat is bought reach, visible to a human in under a second and precisely what F1 measures numerically.

states: LOADING — 12 skeleton `.ptk` rows using the existing `skel` 1.2s keyframe. Header and control strip render immediately and are interactive. Count chip shows `…`.
EMPTY (quiet) — `.noresult` block: 'No posts currently qualify.' plus a --dim second line stating LAST TICK age and the gate breakdown, so 'quiet night' is never confusable with 'we are broken'.

EMPTY (broken) — LAST TICK > 120s: amber `.scoring-paused-banner` reading 'PIPELINE STALE — last snapshot 6m ago. Ranks are frozen.' The board keeps rendering the last committed tick with all HEAT cells dimmed.
ERROR — board query failed: red-bordered banner, retry button, last successful tick still rendered from cache with an explicit `as of 14:22` stamp.

INGESTION GAP DETECTED — affected rows carry an amber `FROZEN` chip, HEAT goes --dim, ACCEL renders `—`. EWMA state is frozen, not decayed. The earliness ledger marks the window unmeasurable rather than counting it as a win.

MEME SCORING PAUSED — existing `.scoring-paused-banner` verbatim: 'Meme scoring paused / Anthropic budget exhausted — new viral posts will not appear until scoring resumes.' Existing rows keep updating.
COLD START (single snapshot) — ACCEL `—`, sparkline blank, HEAT rendered but with a --dim asterisk; the row cannot enter until 2 ticks unless the rate_LCB escape hatch fires.
CENSORED ENTRY / ALREADY HOT — amber `ALREADY HOT` chip, E=0.70 applied, AGE cell shows no lead figure, excluded from the earliness denominator.
SECOND WAVE — cyan `2ND WAVE` `.lc-pill`, re-entry with ENTER_TICKS still enforced, original posted_at retained so the age penalty stays honest.
UNVERIFIED COIN MATCH (UNSURE) — Buy suppressed; `Create coin` remains primary; candidate mint shown in --muted as `$KANG · unverified` with no one-tap path to buying.
ABSTAIN — same treatment. The mint is SHOWN, labelled, non-actionable. Abstain never means hide.
STORY WITH NO COIN — the normal case on this board. `Create coin`, prefilled from suggested_ticker/suggested_name/media.

BRAND-NEW TOKEN, NO MARKET DATA — when a story's coin is <10 min old, any mcap/liquidity render as `—` in --dim, never `$0` and never a reassuring green. A grey dash is honest; a missing chip reads as 'fine'.
COINABILITY no_create (D3 tier 2) — public tragedy, ongoing disaster: row ranks and displays normally, action cell shows `NOT MINTABLE` with a one-line reason. Discussable, not mintable.
COINABILITY blocked (D3 tier 1) — identifiable private individual, death, violence against a named person, minors: the row never enters the board and never enters the rail.
WALLET NOT CONNECTED — buttons render true labels, fully enabled; click opens Privy then completes the intent.
FROZEN (pointer inside the table) — 1px inset rgba(61,224,255,.25) ring on `.ttable`, control strip shows `PAUSED · 3 QUEUED`. Values keep ticking; positions do not move.
AUTHOR CAPPED — a third row from the same author is suppressed; the author's highest row gains a --dim foot line `+2 more from @handle`, so the cap is visible rather than silent.
MEDIA FETCH FAILED — falls to the PAL gradient placeholder + `no media` chip. Never a stock-photo substitute.
STALE HTTP FALLBACK — Broadcast disconnected, jittered polling active: the `.lz` dot turns amber and `.rail-status` reads `polling fallback`, with row age surfaced from the response Age header.

dataContract:
EXISTS TODAY AND IS USED AS-IS
──────────────────────────────
narrative_posts — id, platform, handle, text, posted_at (bigint unix MS — the
  age source; never first_seen_at), views, likes, retweets, replies, quotes,
  followers, media_url, media_type, image, narrative_id, platform_post_id,
  first_seen_at, last_snapshot_at, snapshot_tier, tracking_status,
  filter_label, notable, sample_replies, pruned_at
post_snapshots — post_id, captured_at, views, likes, retweets, replies,
  quotes, bookmarks, unavailable, raw
post_meme_scores — post_id, meme_score, suggested_ticker, suggested_name,
  reason, views_velocity, engagement_velocity, velocity, model, scored_at
narratives — id, title, blurb, lifecycle, display_eligible, organic_score,
  combined_views, views_velocity, engagement_velocity, accel, lead_time_min,
  platforms, gate_reason
narrative_tickers — ticker, name, mcap, liquidity, vol24h, holders, age_min,
  canonical, first_deployed, mint_ca, safety, smart_money
worker_cycle_log / worker_budget_state — for LAST TICK and the paused banner

⚠ DOES NOT EXIST — every one of these is required and must be flagged
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. post_heat (new table, PK post_id)
     heat numeric, base numeric, presented_heat int,
     rate_lcb_views numeric, rate_lcb_reshares numeric, rate_lcb_norm numeric,
     s_fast numeric, s_slow numeric, ewma_updated_at timestamptz,
     burst numeric, accel_branching numeric,
     organic_o numeric, organic_features jsonb,
     ct_pickup_count int, ct_first_seen_at timestamptz,
     lifecycle text, lifecycle_ticks int, v_peak numeric,
     censored_entry bool, second_wave bool, frozen bool,
     ticks_qualified int, computed_at timestamptz
   Index: (heat desc) where computed_at > now() - interval '10 min'
   NOTHING in the ranking formula has a home today. post_meme_scores.velocity
   and narratives.views_velocity are raw deltas computed on views, which is the
   exact base §4.2 rejects.

2. board_state + board_ticks (new)
     board_ticks(tick_id bigserial, lane text, committed_at timestamptz)
     board_state(tick_id, lane, rank int, entity_type text, entity_id uuid,
                 heat numeric, prev_rank int, entered_at timestamptz,
                 pinned_until timestamptz, exit_ticks int)
   Without these there is no rank delta, no ENTER/EXIT tick counting, no
   MAX_MOVE, no PIN_MS, no Δ10m mode, and no rail event log.

3. narrative_posts.coinability enum('normal','no_create','blocked')
   + coinability_reason text + coinability_model text
   D3 has NO representation in the schema at all today. Until it exists the
   never-surface tier cannot be enforced and the board is unshippable.

4. narrative_posts.media_phash bigint  — near-duplicate collapse
   narrative_posts.media_poster_url text — TikTok/X video poster frames.
   media_url on TikTok is not a poster frame; without this every video row
   falls to the gradient placeholder.

5. narrative_posts.followers_at_post int — `followers` is the CURRENT value.
   F4 (views/followers overshoot) computed against a follower count that grew
   because of the viral post is circular.

6. post_derived_subject text + derived_by text — the TikTok hashtag-spam case.

7. platform_norms(platform, window, median_view_rate_24h, median_views_at_age
   jsonb, p95_heat_1h, updated_at) — the rate normaliser, the censored-entry
   detector, and the presented-heat denominator all read this. Hourly pg_cron.

8. author_roster(handle, platform, tier, follower_decile, a0, b0, hit_rate,
   updated_at) — supplies the Gamma-Poisson prior. Without it there is no
   cold start, only nulls.

9. ingest_gaps(source, started_at, ended_at, affected_post_count) — drives the
   FROZEN state and marks windows unmeasurable in the earliness ledger.

10. coin_matches(narrative_id, mint, verdict enum('confirmed','unsure',
    'rejected'), score numeric, evidence jsonb, mint_created_at, matched_at)
    The primary button is a function of a CONFIRMED count that has nowhere to
    live. narrative_tickers has no verdict column and, critically, NO `source`
    column — so an LLM-invented ticker and a real cashtag are indistinguishable
    downstream (cluster.js:310 upsertTickers). That is the live $KANG bug.

11. watchlist(user_id, entity_type, entity_id, created_at) — today the
    watchlist is two in-memory Sets. `.star` on a post row has nowhere to write.

12. Index required: post_snapshots(post_id, captured_at desc) — the sparkline
    lateral does 40 ordered scans per hydration without it.

13. CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE: docs/schema.md lists narrative_tickers.mint_ca,
    but lib/types.ts asserts "There is no mint address column". One of the two
    is stale. The Buy path cannot be built until this is settled.

BOARD HYDRATION QUERY (ISR route, revalidate = 2)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
select p.id, p.platform, p.handle, p.text, p.posted_at, p.followers,
       p.views, p.likes, p.retweets, p.replies, p.quotes,
       p.media_url, p.media_poster_url, p.media_type, p.platform_post_id,
       p.narrative_id, p.coinability,
       h.presented_heat, h.rate_lcb_views, h.rate_lcb_reshares, h.burst,
       h.organic_o, h.lifecycle, h.censored_entry, h.second_wave,
       h.ct_pickup_count, h.frozen,
       m.meme_score, m.suggested_ticker, m.suggested_name,
       b.rank, b.prev_rank, b.entered_at,
       cm.confirmed_count, cm.top_ticker, cm.unsure_ticker,
       s.spark
from board_state b
join narrative_posts p on p.id = b.entity_id
join post_heat h       on h.post_id = p.id
left join post_meme_scores m on m.post_id = p.id
left join lateral (
  select count(*) filter (where verdict='confirmed')            as confirmed_count,
         max(ticker) filter (where verdict='confirmed')          as top_ticker,
         max(ticker) filter (where verdict='unsure')             as unsure_ticker
  from coin_matches where narrative_id = p.narrative_id
) cm on true
left join lateral (
  select array_agg(dv order by captured_at) as spark from (
    select captured_at,
           views - lag(views) over (order by captured_at) as dv
    from post_snapshots where post_id = p.id
    order by captured_at desc limit 9
  ) t where dv is not null
) s on true
where b.lane = 'posts'
  and b.tick_id = (select max(tick_id) from board_ticks where lane='posts')
order by b.rank
limit 40;

REALTIME CONTRACT
─────────────────
Topic `board:posts`, Supabase Broadcast, change-driven, per-client coalescing
to ≤1 frame / 500 ms. Payload:
  { tick: 88214, committed_at,
    changes: [{id, rank, prev_rank, heat, views, rate, burst, lifecycle}],
    enters:  [<full row shape above>],
    exits:   [{id, reason: 'cooling'|'aged'|'gate'|'author_cap'|'collapsed'}] }
Full row only on enter — everything else is a diff.
Drop `replica identity full` from narrative_posts in the same migration
(currently set in worker/schema-realtime.sql); Postgres Changes is disqualified.

REJECTED COLUMNS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT RE-PROPOSED
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
· Separate likes / replies / quotes columns — three raw counts that change no
  decision the RATE and ORG columns don't already answer. They live in the sheet.
· Price / mcap / liquidity on a post row — no coin exists; rendering a market
  column on a pre-coin object is the category error the whole lane exists to avoid.
· A numeric match-confidence percentage — categorical only, next to any
  actionable control (§5.9).
· devHoldingPct / sniperPct / bundlePct — not obtainable from Jupiter or
  DexScreener without first-slot transaction analysis. Render `—`, never green.
buildOrder: 1. MIGRATION ONLY, no UI. Create post_heat, platform_norms, author_roster, board_ticks, board_state, ingest_gaps; add narrative_posts.coinability / coinability_reason / media_phash / media_poster_url / followers_at_post; add the post_snapshots(post_id, captured_at desc) index; drop replica identity full from narrative_posts. Backfill post_heat from seven days of existing post_snapshots. Shippable alone: nothing reads it yet.

2. OFFLINE CONTROL EXPERIMENT, runnable the moment step 1's backfill lands and before any infrastructure is committed. Score seven days of post_snapshots with HN's (P-1)/(T+2)^G alongside the PostHeat formula, judged on early-detection precision: did the top-10 at time t contain posts whose stories produced a >=$100k coin after t. If HN wins, 'HN with hotter constants' was the right answer and steps 3-4 shrink to a one-line score. This is a cheap experiment, not an admission.

3. PIPELINE SCORER. Write the continuous-time EWMA accumulator (S_fast/S_slow with exp(-dt/tau)), the Gamma-Poisson rate_LCB for both views and reshares, the five O features, branching factor, lifecycle with hysteresis, and censored-entry detection into post_heat on every snapshot arrival. Fix the cold-start null at worker/lib/velocity.js:50 to seed rate = views/age. Freeze-not-decay on detected ingest gaps. Pure functions land in features/feed/model/rank.ts with mandatory tests and no mocks.

4. COMMIT_BOARD. pg_cron: heat refresh every 60s, commit_board() every 20s applying EPS_SWAP 0.08 / ENTER_TICKS 2 / EXIT_TICKS 3 / PIN_MS 90000 / MAX_MOVE 5 plus the author cap, story cap and phash dedup; platform_norms hourly. Writes board_state + board_ticks. Verifiable entirely from SQL before any pixel exists.

5. STATIC BOARD. ISR route (revalidate = 2) + the hydration query + the .ptk row component with all eleven columns, sticky .pthd, and the responsive .h collapse. No realtime, no animation, no filters. This is already a shippable product surface: a ranked board that refreshes every two seconds beats a feed that doesn't rank.

6. MEDIA. Poster-frame ingestion, phash computation, the three-case thumbnail (image / video+play / PAL gradient), .srcchip-mini labels, and DELETION of the loremflickr/picsum fabrication chain. TikTok hashtag de-emphasis and the DERIVED subject fallback.

7. CONTROL STRIP. Lane switch, platform chips, age window, sort chips + column-header sort, MEME/ORG threshold popovers, SHOW RISKY (loud), COLLAPSE BY STORY, localStorage persistence, and the 'N hidden by gate' disclosure with its per-reason breakdown.

8. REALTIME. Broadcast channel board:posts with 500ms per-client coalescing, the Map<id,Row> value-update path, .nm-tick-up/down animations, the new-posts pill, freeze-on-hover with the queued-reorder ring, LAST TICK staleness indicator and the stale/polling-fallback states.

9. STORY COLLAPSE + ACTION RESOLUTION. One row per story, the '+N posts' chip, the '-> STORY' chip, stable-key migration from post:<id> to story:<narrative_id>, crossfade on member swap, and the coin-count-derived button with its one-time --ion pulse on transition. Requires coin_matches, which is the story-to-coin workstream's deliverable, not this one's.

10. COINABILITY ENFORCEMENT. Classifier writes narrative_posts.coinability; blocked never enters the board or the rail; no_create renders the NOT MINTABLE chip with a reason. This gates GA — the board cannot ship to the public without D3 enforced.

11. RAIL POSTS MODE. The fourth .railtabs mode, the board-transition event log derived from consecutive board_ticks diffs, pipeline events folded into the same stream, SINCE OPEN and delta-10m toggles.
12. DETAIL SHEET. Extend the existing .pd-sheet with the .pd-rank score-decomposition block and the tall sparkline, plus the deleted-post and unavailable states.
openQuestions: E, the entry-integrity multiplier for censored-entry posts, is set to 0.70 by judgement, not by fit. The step-1 backfill can settle it: measure what fraction of >=$100k coin outcomes came from posts we first saw already large. If that fraction is high, E should be closer to 1.0 and the honest penalty belongs only in the earliness ledger, not in the ranking. The prior question is sharper: should censored-entry posts be on this board at all, or is 'we were late to this one' a different surface?

Does the crypto-pickup penalty C apply at post level? Section 4.2 defines it for narratives, and the ~300-account CT poller currently detects pickup at story granularity. A post is frequently quoted by CT before it is ever clustered, which is exactly the moment the edge dies. Applying C at post level requires per-post quote detection from the poller — a real scope addition to the pipeline, not a UI decision.

Is there a poster-frame URL anywhere in the TikTok or X ingest payload? If not, every video row on this board is a gradient placeholder forever, which materially changes how the POST cell should be laid out (the thumbnail may not earn its 44px).

Legal read required before ship: does a `Create coin` button in an adjacent grid cell, separated by a divider, count as a third-party action control 'attached to' a rendered post under X's display requirements? The answer changes the row layout, not the copy. Assume the strict reading until counsel says otherwise.

Is `followers` populated for TikTok, Reddit, Farcaster and Telegram, or only X? F4 (views/followers overshoot) silently degrades to f4=1 on every non-X row if not, which means the organic multiplier is weaker on exactly the platform where the meme most often originates.

The presented-heat denominator is p95_heat over 1 hour. On a quiet night an hour may contain fewer than 40 eligible posts, making p95 a single noisy observation and every row read 100. Fall back to a 6h window when n < 60, or accept the noise?

Should the Posts lane be the default landing lane, or Stories? 'Front door' and 'the surface where earliness is felt' both argue Posts, but a normie arriving from TikTok is better served by a story with a coin already attached. This may want to be a per-user default rather than a product-wide one.
The 40-row cap is inherited from the stories board. A posts board is inherently higher-volume — is 40 the right cap, or does the posts lane want 60 with the gate tightened to compensate?

Near-duplicate collapse at hamming(phash) <= 6 is a guess. The threshold needs calibration against the actual repost swarms in the existing corpus before it ships, because too tight collapses genuinely different posts about the same event and too loose leaves the board as twelve copies of one video.
priorArt: Hacker News (P-1)/(T+2)^1.8 — the age-penalty shape PostHeat inherits, and the offline control the whole formula must beat before the infrastructure is committed. Its structural limitation, monotone non-increasing once inflow stops, is the entire argument for the EWMA burst term.

Reddit _confidence() / Wilson lower bound — the mechanism reused as rate_LCB: treat the count as sample size and rank the lower bound, not the point estimate. Applied to arrival rate rather than to a vote proportion.

Szabo & Huberman early-popularity prediction — the source of the per-author log-linear baseline, and the source of the mis-specification corrected in section 2.4: their homoskedasticity is with respect to popularity level at a fixed observation pair, not with respect to age.

SEISMIC self-exciting point process — what the branching factor R-hat approximates at count-only cost. Proper SEISMIC needs a retweeters call per post per interval and would exceed the entire ingest budget.
Photon's freeze-on-hover — borrowed verbatim, because it is the only interaction that makes a 20-second-committing board usable with a mouse in it.
TweetDeck's column model — the precedent for a dense, persistently-live, multi-lane social board that traders already have muscle memory for.

Axiom / DexScreener new-pairs boards — the density and rank-column conventions this lane matches, and the precedent it deliberately breaks: both start at the coin, so their columns are all market data, which is exactly the set of columns a pre-coin object cannot have.

Jupiter organicScore — the coin lane's organic signal, and the cautionary precedent for O: Jupiter flags a wallet non-organic only on identifiable patterns and defaults everything else to organic, so its error is systematically false-positive. O is floored at 0.15 rather than 0 for the same reason in reverse.
